headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: EBAY, SNDK, META, IONQ, LITE Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Here are some of the companies making headlines in midday trading. Memory stocks – Shares of memory chip companies slid after China's CXMT said it will begin producing next-generation memory chips that will compete for market share with U.S. and Korean companies. Micron Technology lost about 3%, as did Seagate Technology . Western Digital fell more than 2% and Sandisk lost more than 5%. The Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) shed 4%. eBay — The e-commerce company jumped more than 5% after Morgan Stanley dubbed eBay a top pick and lifted its price target to $132, suggesting nearly 18% upside. The firm estimates that the $27 billion live selling market – which involves selling products in real time through a livestream – is "driving 40%+ of EBAY's growth." Meta Platforms — Shares gained more than 3% after Meta unveiled it s new artificial intelligence model , dubbed Muse Wonder. Speculation on the rollout, codenamed Watermelon, was heating up earlier on Monday after Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang posted on social media platform X "vibes kinda good," followed by a watermelon emoji. Optical stocks — Investors took a few chips off the table after artificial intelligence plays saw a rebound last Friday. Ciena was last down more than 8%, while Lumentum slid 9%. Applied Optoelectronics fell 6%. Salesforce — The stock rose almost 2% after a Bank of America double upgrade to buy from underperform. The bank argued that artificial intelligence should not disrupt, rather "deepen dependence" on the software name. First Solar — Shares gained 2% after Truist upgraded the solar name to buy from hold. The bank is confident in the growth and strong demand in the solar market over the coming years, as well as First Solar's pricing power in the industry. Biogen — Shares of Biogen rose nearly 4% after analysts at JPMorgan upgraded the biotech name to overweight from neutral . The firm cited several clinical readouts in 2027 as catalysts for Biogen. SLM — Shares advanced 4% after the company, which deals with the administration of education loans, was upgraded by Morgan Stanley to overweight from equal weight. The stock down 15% year to date is a buying opportunity, Morgan Stanley said, given its favorable valuation. Mattel — The toymaker rose 1% after analysts at Seaport upgraded the stock to buy from neutral. With speculation of a potential takeover swirling, "we think investors are taking a closer look at toy stocks and realizing that there's underappreciated value," the research firm wrote. IonQ — Shares fell more than 8% after the company bought cybersecurity firm Elisity for $1.3 billion . Quantum computing stocks Rigetti Computing and D-Wave Quantum each shed roughly 5% in sympathy. — CNBC's Nick Wells and Tom Rotunno contributed reporting.

headlines.article_text: IonQ to acquire cybersecurity firm Elisity for up to $1.3 billion Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Quantum computing platform IonQ said it will acquire cybersecurity company Elisity in an all-stock deal for up to $1.3 billion, including up to $150 million in performance-based earnouts. The combined entity will give IonQ expanded tools to detect and defend against AI-driven cyberattacks. IonQ's shares are down more than 9% Monday. In this article IONQ Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Sheldon Cooper | Lightrocket | Getty Images Quantum computing platform IonQ said on Monday it will acquire cybersecurity company Elisity in an all-stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion, including up to $150 million in performance-based earnouts. The move is designed to defend against and uncover attackers targeting generative AI large-language models and AI agents, and to protect against emerging quantum threats, the companies said in a press release . "With Elisity and its team as part of IonQ, we will be well positioned to help customers protect critical infrastructure and enterprise networks throughout the transition to the quantum era," Niccolo de Masi, IonQ's chairman and CEO, said in the release. The all-stock deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter, subject to regulatory approval, and would expand the quantum-computing company's cybersecurity portfolio. IonQ shares fell more than 9% in afternoon trading. Other quantum computing stocks, including Rigetti Computing and D-Wave Quantum , also traded lower. Elisity will retain its current leadership, including CEO James Winebrenner. IonQ's stock has surged in recent months amid a buying spree. Most recently, the company bought semiconductor maker SkyWater Technology for $1.8 billion in July. In the past year and a half, IonQ has acquired several quantum companies, most notably U.K.-based quantum computing startup Oxford Ionics . The deal follows two June executive orders from President Donald Trump aimed at building a quantum computer for scientific research by 2028 and protecting government systems from cyber threats. IonQ said in the release that the orders underscored the urgency of preparing for quantum computing threats. But it doesn't come for free. To access the model, users of the Muse personal agent app will need to sign up for a monthly subscription of $20 or $100. The release underscores Meta's efforts to create new AI-derived revenue sources outside of its core online ad business . Meta AI chief Alexandr Wang said in an interview on Monday that the company developed Muse Wonder, codenamed Watermelon, to improve the capabilities of "personal and professional agents" so they don't stumble on tasks like booking dinner reservations and checking for availabilities. "When you do real-world tasks, you're going to get roadblocks and you're going to get things that come up or various setbacks," Wang said. "We specifically tried to train the model to be able to try other approaches instead of stalling and then checking back in with the user at any time." Mark Zuckerberg, chief executive officer of Meta Platforms Inc., reveals the Muse Charm device during the Meta Connect event in Menlo Park, California, US, on Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. Minh Connors | Bloomberg | Getty Images Meta said in a blog post that the latest model "offers our strongest safeguards to date" against "cyber misuse." Those protections only come with the paid model for now. Muse shot up to the top of Apple's App Store after Meta introduced the AI agent app last month. The app is free, with subscription plans available for more usage. Wang said Meta's AI team has been monitoring for agent-related "incidents or issues" with Muse in order to understand problems and resolve them. Some users have complained on social media that the agent accessed personal messages without authorization, which the company has disputed . Meta is trying to better inform people of how to use the app to avoid certain problems, Wang said. "I think there are certainly instances users have authorized various communications or whatnot earlier in a conversation, and then may have forgotten about that," Wang said. He added that the company is educating users on such matters "to ensure that consumers can trust the product going forward." Muse Wonder will also be available to coders who pay to access the company's related Meta Model API . Wang said that offering will cost more than the standard subscriptions because it is a "much larger model and at frontier level." He said it will still be priced "meaningfully below" leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic. An even more powerful variant of Meta's latest model, dubbed Muse Wonder Full, will only be available to developers who sign up to the company's software engineering focused Muse Code AI agent under a $50 or $200 a month subscription plan.
